title: Request ancestry enricher and edge-router integration for cross-service trace stitching
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight request-ancestry enrichment layer in our edge routers and language SDKs to reliably reconstruct cross-service request trees for tracing and post-hoc debugging. Motivation: many production incidents show gaps in parent-child relationships when requests traverse proxies, CDN edges, serverless functions and async queues. Current traceparent/baggage propagation is uneven across customer infra and mobile/native SDKs, causing partial traces and poor root-cause analysis.

What we will deliver: 
1) Edge enricher: an opt-in module for our edge/router that adds a compact ancestry header (rw-anc-v1) encoding an ancestry chain of up to 6 hop IDs with per-hop meta (role, region, short-ts). The header will be encoded as a compact, URL-safe base64 payload with TTL and size limit enforcement.
2) SDK middleware: language SDK instrumentation that reads rw-anc-v1 + existing trace headers, appends a local hop entry and emits both standard OTEL-compatible trace headers and the enriched ancestry header. SDKs will ensure minimal allocations and fall back to a single-hop header when request size budget is exhausted.
3) Backwards compatibility shim: translation layer at the edge to interoperate with traceparent/B3/W3C. If incoming traffic has only traceparent, we synthesize a minimal ancestry entry so stitchers downstream can reconstruct lineage.
4) Telemetry and dashboards: new observability metrics and dashboards tracking ancestry coverage, header size distribution, drop rate, and ancestry reconstruction success rate. Alerts for sudden drops in ancestry coverage or header bloat.

Design constraints and decisions: 
- Header size budget: target 512 bytes max (including existing tracing headers). Will clamp to 6 hop entries; older hops evicted in FIFO.
- Privacy/security: no user PII should ever be placed in the ancestry header. Hop IDs are derived from service instance ID + truncated HMAC with current key. All bytes are opaque to customers unless they own the private keys.
- Performance budget: instrumentation must add <1% p50 latency on our SDK hot paths. Edge enricher must process >50k rps per instance at p95 CPU budget.
- Failure modes: if header parsing fails or TTL expired, we fallback to plain traceparent propagation. Enricher will emit a metric and increment a per-route "ancestry.parse_error" counter.

Compatibility: supports hosted API, Dedicated edge routers, and Private deployments. Will provide config toggles for anonymization, TTL, and max_hops in private customer configs.

Rollout plan: 
- Spike/prototype (this ticket) -> implement prototype in edge dev cluster + nodejs and python SDK middleware.
- Canary: enable for 5% of inbound traffic to edge-router in us-west-2 for 48h. Observe ancestry_coverage and 95th latency change.
- Ramp: 25% -> 100% with 24h holds.
- SDKs: release SDK middleware as opt-in in 0.1.0 packages, then flip default after one cycle of adoption and compatibility checks.

Monitoring and success criteria: 
- Ancestry coverage >= 90% for internal services within 7 days of rollout.
- Header size P95 < 420 bytes.
- No more than 1% relative increase in p50 latency for instrumented SDK calls.
- Dashboard: ancestry.reconstruct_success_rate, ancestry.parse_errors, ancestry.header_size_p{50,95,99}, ancestry.coverage_by_route.

Open questions / trade-offs: 
- How to support long-lived async queues where full ancestry may exceed size budget? Proposal: add compressed breadcrumb entries only at enqueue/dequeue points and a separate queue-segment token referencing server-side retained lineage.
- Key rotation for hop ID HMACs: need KMS integration with an automatic rotation plan; will reuse platform KMS policy to avoid additional secret management overhead.

Artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/request-ancestry-v1 (draft), prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/5421 (edge enricher), SDK prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/198 (middleware), perf bench: https://app.internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/ancestry-perf
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Created spike ticket after postmortem for INC-20260128 highlighted 2/3 missing parent spans across CDN edge. Proposed compact ancestry header to preserve lineage through opaque proxies.

2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Completed prototype of edge enricher (branch edge/ancestry-proto). Able to encode 4 hops within 256 bytes. Initial perf on dev cluster shows ~0.3ms per-request overhead at 10k rps.

2026-03-06 - Design review (PM/SEC): Security flagged HMAC key handling and requested KMS-based key rotation and a strict no-PII policy. Updated design to store only opaque truncated HMACs + service role bit. Added security_review_required flag on ticket.
2026-03-08 - QA: Added unit tests for header eviction logic and TTL expiry. Found edge case where gzip-ing downstream altered header order; fixed by canonical encoding step in enricher.

2026-03-10 - Perf: Benchmarked NodeJS SDK middleware; allocations optimized to reusable buffers. p50 added latency is 0.6% at 1000rps synthetic workload. Need language SDKs (python/go/java) to replicate low-overhead approach.

2026-03-12 - PM feedback (Diego Morales): Add rollout gating metric for ancestry.coverage_by_customer so we can pause for customers who opt-out. Also requested a migration guide for private deployments.

2026-03-14 - Liam Chen: Opened edge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/5421 and SDK PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/198. Preparing canary config for us-west-2; adding dashboard panels and alerts (ancestry.parse_errors > 0.5% triggers paging).
